newsitem.title: USA: Maine lawmakers, governor at odds over budget gap.
newsitem.headline: Maine lawmakers, governor at odds over budget gap.

text.p: A report prepared for the Maine Legislature estimates the state will face a $363 million gap in the next two-year budget, about $60 million less than Gov. Angus King's staff projects.

Lawmakers who met with administration officials Thursday agreed that significant spending cuts will have to be made, but believe the administration's budget projections have made the situation look worse than it is.

Rep. George Kerr, D-Old Orchard, Appropriations Committee co-chair, argued officials were over-estimating the spending requirements in areas such general state aid to education and law enforcement for the budget that will begin July 1997.

Finance Commissioner Janet Waldron, who has projected the gap will be about $420 million, said the situation has been made worse by lawmakers' approval of a cap on revenue from personal income and a repeal of a tax on hospitals and nursing homes.

"The tax reductions total about $372 million so it completely off-sets any new revenue growth by a sizable amount (and) that's before you get to any increased expenditure items," Waldren told a committee hearing.
Waldren said the administration would fight any effort to balance the budget through income tax surcharges or with "one- time gimicks" that would push the problem in to future budgets.
